page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c1.large is a compute-focused virtual machine instance built on the x86_64 architecture and hosted on the KVM hypervisor. The configuration provides 8 dedicated vCPUs alongside 16.0 GB of system memory, resulting in a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware GPU acceleration is not present on this instance type.

The instance does not include bundled local storage, requiring persistent operational workloads to depend entirely on network-attached block storage volumes. In addition, ecs.c1.large includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, necessitating external network routing or elastic IP allocations for outward-facing communication.

With dedicated CPU core allocation and a hardware profile tailored toward compute execution rather than large memory buffers, resource density is prioritized for CPU-bound tasks. This configuration is well-aligned with workloads such as distributed batch compute jobs, compilation tasks, web serving clusters, and background worker services.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c1.large is a compute-focused instance type within the ecs.c1 family, utilizing the x86_64 architecture under the KVM hypervisor. The virtual machine is equipped with 8 dedicated vCPUs and 16.0 GB of memory, delivering a dense 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per core. It operates without bundled local storage and includes zero integrated GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses, relying on external network-attached volumes for data retention and network infrastructure for external routing. Due to its dedicated processor allocation and lean memory footprint, the instance is positioned for CPU-intensive processing tasks where memory overhead is moderate. Primary workload fits include batch job processing, parallel compilation pipelines, web application serving, and distributed compute worker tasks.
